definition: Aesthetic appreciation is the kind of favorable response used in contrast with moral approbation. Unlike moral approbation, it does not involve judging a person’s conduct or character in terms of merit or demerit.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Approbation; pinned source text

reasons: The packet only supplies a contrast with moral approbation; it does not directly define aesthetic appreciation as a “favorable response,” so that substantive characterization is unsupported.

The packet does not define “aesthetic appreciation” itself as a “kind of favorable response”; it only gives a definition of “moral approbation” and then states a contrast/differentia involving merit or demerit.

Because the definition’s first substantive clause (“the kind of favorable response used in contrast with moral approbation”) is not explicitly supported in the provided text, the overall definition is not fully defensible from the packet.
